title: What's the Best VoC Solution for Enterprise? 6 Platforms Matched to the Job
summary: The best enterprise VoC solution depends on the job: surveys, operational response, calls, B2B accounts, scattered channels, or explaining why scores move.
body_markdown:
Enterprise voice of customer (VoC) programs rarely fail at collection. They fail when a leadership team asks why a score moved and nobody can answer quickly.[McKinsey](https://www.mckinsey.com/capabilities/growth-marketing-and-sales/our-insights/prediction-the-future-of-cx) surveyed more than 260 customer experience (CX) leaders at US companies. 93% use a survey-based metric as their primary measure of CX performance. Only 6% are confident their measurement system can support both strategic and tactical decisions.


The best VoC solution for an enterprise is the one built for the job your program is struggling with. Qualtrics is strongest for running survey programs at scale. Medallia is strongest for operational response. Thematic is strongest for explaining why a score moved, with every finding traced to the comments behind it. Chattermill suits teams whose main problem is feedback scattered across channels, Verint suits contact-center-led programs, and CustomerGauge suits B2B account-based NPS.


Below is each platform matched to that job, with one real limitation for each. Thematic is on this list, so treat that as a stated bias and check the criteria yourself.


## The shortlist at a glance


**If your main problem is...** **Look at** **Watch out for**


Explaining why NPS or CSAT moved, in a way leadership will accept Thematic Doesn't collect feedback; sits on your existing tools


Feedback scattered across many channels and markets Chattermill Returns the biggest themes, not score attribution


Running and distributing surveys at scale Qualtrics XM Text analytics hard to audit; taxonomies drift


Responding to individual customers fast (cases, alerts) Medallia Analysis is the weaker half


Recorded calls and agent quality Verint Built for agent operations, not cross-channel VoC


Account-level NPS in B2B, tied to revenue CustomerGauge Thinner analysis layer


One market note before the detail. Press Ganey Forsta acquired InMoment in 2025, and Qualtrics completed its[$6.75 billion acquisition of Press Ganey Forsta](https://www.qualtrics.com/news/qualtrics-to-invest-6-75-billion-in-press-ganey-forsta-acquisition-to-advance-ai-powered-experience-management/) on[May 18, 2026](https://www.cmswire.com/customer-experience/after-uncertainty-qualtrics-finalizes-6-75-billion-acquisition-of-press-ganey-forsta/) . InMoment, Forsta and Qualtrics XM Discover (formerly Clarabridge) now sit under one owner, so they count as one vendor on an enterprise shortlist.


## 1. Thematic: for explaining why a score moved


**Thematic is a customer intelligence layer for enterprise teams whose reporting gets scrutinized.** It analyzes surveys, support tickets, call transcripts and reviews together, builds themes from the data rather than a prebuilt industry model, and links every theme to the comments behind it. Its[Score Change Waterfall](https://getthematic.com/insights/quantify-themes-moved-nps-score) shows how many points each theme added to or removed from a metric between two periods.


For enterprise security reviews, Thematic holds[SOC 2 Type II certification](https://getthematic.com/product/security-and-compliance) , does not use customer data to train models for other clients, and supports SAML single sign-on and role-based access.


At[Mitre 10](https://getthematic.com/insights/humanising-hardware-how-mitre10-made-voice-of-customer-actionable-with-thematic) , a three-person insights team handles about 20,000 comments a month across 84 stores and found stock availability was taking half an NPS point off the overall score.


**Limitation:** Thematic doesn't collect feedback. You keep your survey platform and helpdesk.


## 2. Chattermill: for scattered channels


**Chattermill fits when the core problem is consolidation.** If feedback lands in Zendesk, Trustpilot, survey tools and call recordings across several markets, and nobody sees it in one place, it does that unification work well.


**Limitation:** what comes back is a ranked list of the period's biggest themes. That is different from explaining how much each theme moved a score, which is usually what a CFO asks for next. See our[Chattermill alternatives](https://getthematic.com/insights/chattermill-alternatives-and-competitors) for more detail.


## 3. Qualtrics XM: for the survey program itself


**Qualtrics is the strongest platform here for building, distributing and managing surveys at scale,** and most enterprises buy it for that reason.


**Limitation:** predefined taxonomies drift as customers change how they talk, the text analytics is hard to audit, and add-on modules plus professional services push the real cost past the license line. Many teams keep Qualtrics for collection and add an analysis layer on top. See[Qualtrics alternatives for feedback analytics](https://getthematic.com/insights/best-qualtrics-alternatives-feedback-analytics) .


## 4. Medallia: for operational response


**Medallia is built for operational CX:** case management, alerting, dashboards and broad capture. For teams whose job is responding to individual customers quickly, it remains a strong choice.


**Limitation:** building a defensible answer to "why did the score move?" is slow inside it. For many teams,[keeping Medallia and fixing the analytics layer](https://getthematic.com/insights/top-medallia-alternatives) beats a full platform swap.


## 5. Verint: for contact-center-led programs


**Verint goes deepest on recorded calls,** with speech analytics, agent quality and workforce engagement at its center.


**Limitation:** that focus is agent operations. If insights and product teams need surveys, reviews and tickets read alongside calls, it isn't shaped for that. See[Verint alternatives](https://getthematic.com/insights/verint-alternatives) .


## 6. CustomerGauge: for B2B account-based NPS


**CustomerGauge ties account NPS directly to revenue** and measures every stakeholder in an account, not a single contact. For B2B programs where the account is the unit of analysis, that matters.


**Limitation:** it tells you which accounts are at risk better than it tells you what to change. See[CustomerGauge alternatives](https://getthematic.com/insights/best-customergauge-alternatives) .


## How should an enterprise choose?


Ask these four questions in every demo, ideally inside a[structured proof of concept](https://getthematic.com/insights/evaluate-ai-feedback-analytics-poc) on your own data:


1. **Where does your program break today?** If collection works and the trouble starts at "why," you need an analysis layer, not another suite. Our guide to[what customer intelligence platforms enterprise CX teams use](https://getthematic.com/insights/customer-intelligence-platforms-enterprise-cx-teams) covers the suite-versus-layer decision in more depth.
2. **Can you click from a number to the comments that produced it?** Ask to see it live, not in a screenshot.
3. **Can it tell you how many points each theme contributed to a score change?** A ranked list of top themes is a weaker answer.
4. **What does the full annual cost include?** Ask for add-on modules, professional services, volume tiers and seat charges in writing.


## What's the short answer?


The best VoC solution for enterprise depends on the job: Qualtrics for survey programs, Medallia for operational response, Verint for calls, CustomerGauge for B2B accounts, Chattermill for scattered channels, and Thematic for explaining why scores move with evidence leadership can check. Most enterprises already collect plenty of feedback, so the gap is usually analysis. For the wider market, including survey builders and social listening tools, see our[guide to voice of customer tools](https://getthematic.com/insights/voice-of-customer-tools) .
